in_greek.name: Ιουλίνη
in_greek.meaning: Ιουλίνη σημαίνει γεννημένη στον μήνα Ιούλιο
in_greek.long_meaning: Ιουλίνη είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από το ρωμαϊκό όνομα Ιούλιος, που σημαίνει 'νεότερος' ή 'γεννημένος τον Ιούλιο'. Το όνομα Ιούλιος ήταν συνηθισμένο στην αρχαία Ρώμη και συνδέονταν με τον ρωμαϊκό θεό Δία. Οι χριστιανοί υιοθέτησαν το όνομα Ιουλίνη ως σύμβολο της σύνδεσής τους με την χριστιανική κοινότητα και την ρωμαϊκή-χριστιανική παράδοση.

data.cultural_impact: The name Juliana was widespread among the ancient Romans, especially those of high social status. The name was also popular among early Christians, as it was associated with the virtue of youth and innocence. In many cultures including the Latin, Greek, and Spanish cultures, the name Juliana is still used and revered. Interestingly, the apple blossom is often used as a symbol for the name Juliana, primarily because apple blossoms appear youthful and delicate.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, the name Juliana holds great spiritual significance. St. Juliana de Cornillon is a well-known saint who is believed to have lived in the late 13th century. She is renowned for her visions of a prophecy that foretold the Battle of the Golden Spurs, a pivotal moment in the history of Belgium. St. Juliana is celebrated as the patron saint of those seeking spiritual visions and guidance. The name Juliana is also associated with the virtues of purity and innocence, as it was often given to children named in remembrance of the Virgin Mary. Thus, the name Juliana represents the spiritual qualities of youthfulness, purity, and innocence.
